### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s).

**25** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 05ab9ef895261d5c5f06ec2a5714eb71bd6b61d9`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `master_detail (literal, 33 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 05ab9ef895261d5c5f06ec2a5714eb71bd6b61d9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `94ae00844bbeb3adf51e6d127b26cba7481f7460` — the merge of head `4daa50d71fad5e0cbe4fce2ec2f0b1dd4e436cd7` into base `05ab9ef895261d5c5f06ec2a5714eb71bd6b61d9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 94ae00844bbeb3adf51e6d127b26cba7481f7460 && git checkout 94ae00844bbeb3adf51e6d127b26cba7481f7460
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 05ab9ef895261d5c5f06ec2a5714eb71bd6b61d9 4daa50d71fad5e0cbe4fce2ec2f0b1dd4e436cd7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 05ab9ef895261d5c5f06ec2a5714eb71bd6b61d9 && git merge --no-ff 4daa50d71fad5e0cbe4fce2ec2f0b1dd4e436cd7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 05ab9ef895261d5c5f06ec2a5714eb71bd6b61d9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 05ab9ef895261d5c5f06ec2a5714eb71bd6b61d9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

It queues after one `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` PASS on this head (the published-schema face: `stack.zod.ts`) and a green head.
- Card: #23210, claim `6163383778`, dev report `6165736147`.
- Rulings of record: triage `6142996061` and regrade `6163015687`.

**1. Shape** (read on GitHub, not from the report):
- Draft, base `main`. Line 1 is `Fixes #23210` and line 3 is `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; no other closing keyword sits beside a card number.
- 8 files (`+923 / -40`). `check-governed-merges --pr 23454` reads NOT governed (963 lines).
- The changeset, read sentence by sentence against the diff:
  - It bumps `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/lint` minor, BREAKING.
  - Its FROM → TO rows match the pins: the card's stack, the demoted master, and the prebuilt artifact.
  - Its remedy line and its "Unchanged" list match the code: unseen targets, an already-refused object reported once, the equal-`priority` tie in `packages[]`, and no stored row.
  - The ADR-0087 disposition is `registered cbp-extension-merged-master-refused`, a new step-18 entry with `relevantWhen: stack-declares objectExtensions`.
  - "No export, signature or error code" holds: `check:api-surface` reports the surface unchanged, and the diff adds no `export`.

**2. Premises, measured by the dev** (the registry probe, not committed):
- **H1:** fields merge by name, and a later writer replaces the whole field. `sharingModel` on an extend body is not carried.
- **H2:** `extend` matches by exact name. `cbpx__cbpx_line` never merges into `cbpx_line`.
- **H3:** with `packages[]`, an extension in any body judges an object in any body, and top-level `objectExtensions` are not read, because the engine registers only the bodies' extensions.
- **H4:** `os validate` parses before its rule table, so the card's stack stops at the parse. The lint's input keeps `objectExtensions`.
- **H5:** the issue sits at the deciding extension's `fields`, with the declared control's message byte-equal.
- Seat spot-read of `applyControlledByParentExtensionGate`:
  - extensions are sorted by `priority`, then by package position;
  - a target two bodies declare reads as `null` and is unjudged;
  - a base that is already refused is skipped;
  - a key two writers set at one `priority` skips the target;
  - the chain is `applyApiEndpointGates` → `applyPermissionSetOwnerBindingGate` → the new gate, as on `main`.

**3. Gates:**
- Check-runs on `4daa50d71` at this act: 18 success, 6 skipped, 14 in progress, 0 failures. The queue waits for green on its own.
- Locally, `dispatch-gates --ran` accounts for 91 families: 89 run, and 2 NOT MEASURED.
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exits 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET. It is a Build Core step.
  - `type-check-debt` is owed to CI.
- `check:dev-prereqs` exits 1 for missing `dist/` outside the cli closure: a local precondition, not a verdict.
- Ablations A1 (the `.superRefine`) and A2 (the lint call) turn their pin files red, 9 failed each; on restore, the blob equals HEAD.

**4. Deviations, accepted:**
- **Surface widening.** `semantic-relevance.test.ts` (the reviewed `relevantWhen` enumeration, 25 → 26) and `validate-security-posture.test.ts` (the #5017 receiver tables) are pins that the entry and the lint edit feed.
- **Two pin runs off the lock**, while the lock was contended. Both were re-measured under the lock, and no verdict rests on them.
- **The model-free commit trailers** follow AGENTS.md.

**5. Out of scope:** two Acceptance notes, `carrier: none`, not filed. Both stay as Acceptance notes.
- **The `os explain` text** (`rule-explanations.ts`) for the two `security-controlled-by-parent-*` rules describes the declared object only. Its remedy (keep one master, make every other parent a `lookup`) stays right for an extension. That is a missing sentence, not a wrong one, so filing gate ① does not take it.
- **A malformed non-array `packages`** now throws `INVALID_ARTIFACT_PACKAGES` from the lint too, as its sibling readers do. That applies to unparsed input only.

**6. Landing:**
- Tier S, through the ordinary queue, after the contract review PASS on this head and an all-green head.
- The prebuilt-artifact row ("refused at load; rebuild it") widens the failure from one object that failed closed to the whole artifact's load. The changeset names it, no producer writes the shape today, and the contract review judges it.

Head-sha: `4daa50d71fad5e0cbe4fce2ec2f0b1dd4e436cd7`

Inputs: card #23210 (body; triage `6142996061`, regrade `6163015687`, claim `6163383778`, os-dev-report `6165736147`, the seat's pointer `6165795039`); PR #23454 (body, 8-file list, comments `6165709047` and the seat record `6165781809`, the net diff against `main` at the head: merge-base `a7a135dc2`, +923 / -40); the 39 check-runs on the head; committed source read with `git show` / `git grep` on `origin/main` (`2d2e3ce43`) and `origin/claude/issue-23210-extension-master-detail` (`4daa50d71`). The seat record was judged, not adopted. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) The narrowing — right.** `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` gains `applyControlledByParentExtensionGate`, chained third after `applyApiEndpointGates` and `applyPermissionSetOwnerBindingGate` (`stack.zod.ts:2037-2040`), so `defineStack` (`buildDefinedStack` → `safeParse` → `StackSchemaInvalidError`, 422), `os validate` (`validate.ts:349`), `os build`, `os verify`, the lint scorer and the artifact load (`metadata/src/plugin.ts:1301-1321`) all refuse a stack whose visible `objectExtensions` leave a `controlled_by_parent` object with anything but exactly one required `master_detail`.

- *The merge is computed as the registry computes it.* Read on `origin/main`: `engine.ts:7779-7797` registers each `manifest.objectExtensions` entry as an `extend` contributor named `ext.extend` verbatim, `namespace: undefined`, `priority = ext.priority ?? 200`; `registry.ts` `registerObject` (extend branch) removes the SAME package's earlier extension of that object before pushing (one per package per target, the later entry replacing the earlier whole), then sorts the contributors by `priority` ascending (`registry.ts:3111`) — a stable sort, so equal priorities keep registration order; `foldExtendersOntoDefinition` → `mergeObjectDefinitions` does `merged.fields = { ...base.fields, ...extension.fields }` — by name, the whole field replaced — and the base is chosen by KIND (`overlay ?? own`), never by priority, so an extender at p50 still folds over the owner. The gate does exactly this: base = the target's own declaration (`sharingModel` is not an `ObjectExtensionSchema` key and `mergeObjectDefinitions` copies `fields` / `validations` / `indexes` / three labels only, so the merged object's `sharingModel` is the target's); `byCarrier.set(carrier, …)` keeps one entry per package, last wins; `ordered` is priority-ascending, carrier-ascending; `merged[key] = field` replaces whole; default 200 matches `ObjectExtensionSchema.priority.default(200)` and the engine's `?? 200`. `defineStack` returns `result.data` (parsed), so what the runtime merges carries the same FieldSchema defaults the refinement judged (`required` omitted = `false` on both sides, and the runtime's `resolveCbpRelation` reads `required === true`, `security-plugin.ts:8294`): no verdict differs between the door and the boot. Package ORDER (`resolveArtifactPackageOrder` → `resolvePluginOrder`, dependency-topological, `@objectstack/core`) is the one input the parse does not have; the gate uses carrier position only to sequence evaluation and to DETECT a tie, never to decide one — judged under (b).
- *Reuse, not a copy.* The refinement imports `controlledByParentMasterRefusal` from `./data/controlled-by-parent-master` (the internal predicate `ObjectSchema`'s own refinement and the v18 stored-row listing already share) and emits `refusal.message` unchanged; the spec pin compares it byte-equal with the directly declared control (`stack-cbp-extension-master.test.ts`). The predicate module is untouched and stays unexported. Right.
- *The issue path names the extension.* `path: [...extension.path, 'fields']` where `extension.path` is `['objectExtensions', i]` or `['packages', j, 'manifest', 'objectExtensions', i]`; blame = the last writer of every key that is a `master_detail` in the declaration or in the merged set, so the line that added the second master or demoted the one is the one located, and an innocent co-writer is not (pinned: "only the extension that wrote a master-relevant key is located"). Right.

**(b) Visibility — right, with one blind spot wider than it needs to be (stated, not a FAIL).**

- *Exact `name` equality with `extend`.* `computeFQN` is the identity (`registry.ts:172`); the extension is keyed by `ext.extend` verbatim and an unmatched spelling opens an ownerless entry the registry skips with a warn ("has extenders but no owner"). The gate's `targets.get(record.extend)` is the same exact-string test; `cbpx__cbpx_line` is pinned unjudged at both doors. Right.
- *`packages[]`.* The engine's `manifest.register` (`objectql/src/plugin.ts:641-700`) registers `resolveArtifactPackageOrder(artifact)` — the BODIES only — then `unclaimedTopLevelObjects(artifact)`, which keeps residual items of `type === 'object'` alone. A multi-package stack's top-level `objectExtensions` therefore reach no `registerApp` and are never merged (they land in the metadata door's residual as `object_extension` items, a type with no registry entry — inert). So "an extension in any body judges an object in any body or a residual top-level object; top-level `objectExtensions` are not read" is the engine's registration, exactly. The residual's carrier is `bodies.length`, matching its registration after every body. Right. (That a top-level extension on a `packages[]` stack is silently inert is a pre-existing ADR-0078-shaped silence outside this card; noted under ③.)
- *The unjudged cases.* (1) An unseen target: honest, stated in the changeset's Unchanged list and the entry's `reason`; the runtime's fail-closed refusal is the backstop, as the card's own Acceptance asks. (2) A target two bodies declare: `registerObject(…, 'own')` from a second package throws `ObjectOwnershipConflictError` (ADR-0029 D3) at registration, so no running stack carries the shape; stated in the code docblock and PR body (not in the changeset's list — a minor omission, not a hole). (3) A target already refused as declared: the per-object refinement refuses the stack whole at `objects.N`; reporting once is right. (4) Two writers tied at one `priority`: reachable (two packages extending one object at the default 200 with one key each), honest — the changeset says "two packages write one field at the same priority … not judged" and the runtime winner is `resolvePluginOrder`, which the spec cannot import without a second ordering mechanism (ADR-0130 D5 forbids one). **Residual:** the skip is per TARGET on a tie on ANY key — a tie on an innocent key (both packages write `note`) leaves a second master added by one of them unjudged, although every ordering yields the same master verdict there and no guess would be needed. Both doors skip identically, so parity holds, and the disclosure's literal wording covers it; the blind spot is honest but coarser than the ordering question requires. Follow-up (not owed here): narrow the tie guard to keys whose competing values differ in master-relevance.

**(c) The lint door — parity holds; the rule is read once, the fold is written twice, and the drift guard is the parity table.** `validateSecurityPosture` gains `pushExtensionMergedCbpFindings`, emitting through the two new shared push sites `pushCbpNoRelation` / `pushCbpAmbiguousRelation`, whose `message` and `hint` strings are byte-identical to the inline pushes the diff removes (compared line by line), so the declared and the merged finding are one wording; the finding sits at `objectExtensions[i].fields` (bracketed) with `where: object "name"`. The fold mirrors the schema's (one per carrier, priority then carrier, whole-field replace, same tie guard, same blame), and the two doors are held to one verdict on 8 shapes with paths normalised (`validate-security-posture-extension-merge.test.ts`). The rule predicate itself is the lint's pre-existing `cbpMasterCandidates` (`required === true`, `reference` present) — the same arrangement the file's own docblock records for the declared object (parse, lint, runtime each read ADR-0055 §1 and tests hold them equal), so this diff adds no NEW second reading of the rule; what it adds is a second copy of the merge, declared in Acceptance note 3 with the reason (exporting the spec's fold or predicate is a published widening the card did not take). Reachability is real: `os validate` / `os build` / `os verify` stop at the parse (`author-time-rules.ts`), but `os lint` hands the normalized stack as the `parsed` tier without parsing (`validate-form-layout.ts:112`), the scorer lints after a failed parse, and the runtime write door runs the rule (`CLI_AND_RUNTIME`). On any stack that parses, both doors see the same values (`priority` 200 and `required` false defaults), so the parity table is the right guard; `packagesOf` and `recordsOf` are the lint's shared readers, not new ones. Right.

**(d) The prebuilt-artifact consequence — right, disclosed, and the prescription reaches its reader by the same channels its sibling uses.** Before: `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.parse` at load passed and one object failed closed. After: the artifact is refused at load. That is the posture `cbp-master-relation-tiers-retired` already set for the same object declared directly, ADR-0055 §1 says fail closed, and accepting at load to fail closed at boot is exactly the declared-vs-enforced silence the card is about; no measured producer writes the shape. Changeset FROM / TO row 3 names it ("refused at load; rebuild it from the corrected source"), and the step-18 entry's `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria` say it in words. The entry's `relevantWhen: { kind: 'stack-declares', keys: ['objectExtensions'] }` is answered by `stackDeclaresVerdict` over the top level AND every `packages[].manifest` body (`chain.ts`), so `os migrate meta` lists the TODO for both authoring shapes and prints `verify:` = the acceptance criterion (`migrate/meta.ts:802`), and `build-upgrade-guide` prints it as "Done when". The loader's own refusal names the object, the `objectExtensions.N.fields` path and the field-level remedy, not the word "rebuild" — the generic posture of every refinement at that door; a 17-labelled artifact meets the ADR-0087 D1 handshake first, which names `migrate meta`. Acceptable.

**(e) Public surface — none added.** The diff's only new `export` is `entry` in `18.cbp-extension-merged-master-refused.ts`, the migration-registry generator's file convention (read by the gitignored `registry.ts`, not a package entry). `applyControlledByParentExtensionGate`, `VisibleObjectExtension`, the three lint helpers and `VisibleExtension` are module-private; `controlledByParentMasterRefusal` stays internal; no signature moves; no error code is added (`STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` is in the ledger at `error-code-ledger.zod.ts:1508`, `INVALID_ARTIFACT_PACKAGES` is `packagesOf`'s existing code). Dev's `check:api-surface` reads unchanged; CI `Type Check · source gates` success; `check:export-origins` has no new origin to judge.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/23210-cbp-extension-merged-master.md`: `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/lint` minor, headed BREAKING — correct under the launch-window convention `check-changeset-no-major` enforces (a `major` is refused; breaking ships as `minor` in lockstep). Both packages narrow: the spec's accept set and the lint's findings.
- ADR-0087 disposition `registered cbp-extension-merged-master-refused`: the right class. No lossless D2 mapping exists (which master stays, and whether a parent becomes a `lookup`, are the owner's decisions), so a D3 semantic entry with no conversion is correct; the id is new at this head and absent at the merge base, so `registered` (not `already-registered`) is the honest marker, and `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main` passed locally and in `Lint & Repo Gates`. The step-18 file carries `id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria` in the sibling entries' form, and `relevantWhen` on the one key an author can write the surface under (both shapes, per (d)). The reviewed enumeration `semantic-relevance.test.ts` moves 25 to 26 (18: 20 to 21) with the new key — the pin that makes an unenumerated entry red.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — present in the claim, PR body line 3 and the changeset, and true: no key is added to any published payload.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report `6165736147`: `open_questions: []`; `premise_still_valid: true`. Every flag read.
- Out-of-scope note 1, `os explain` text (`rule-explanations.ts`) for the two `security-controlled-by-parent-*` rules describing the declared object only — correctly a note, not a defect owed here. Its rule statement and remedy ("keep `master_detail` on the ONE master, every other parent a `lookup`") stay true for a merged object; the one sentence that no longer covers the merged case ("`ObjectSchema.create()` makes every `master_detail` on such an object required") is about the declared object and remains true of it, since `ObjectExtensionSchema` forces nothing and an extension's `master_detail` without `required: true` is not a second master at the parse, the lint or the runtime (all three read `required === true`). Missing sentence, not a false one; carrier none is acceptable, and a one-line follow-up on the owning seat's lane is the right place.
- Out-of-scope note 2, `validateSecurityPosture` now throwing `INVALID_ARTIFACT_PACKAGES` on a present non-array `packages` — correctly a note. Ruling A on #15293 makes every reader refuse that shape; `validate-object-references` / `validate-translation-references` / `validate-mapping-target-fields` already throw it through the same `packagesOf` on the same unparsed intake, `runAuthoringRules` catches nothing, so the door's behaviour on that input is unchanged; the schema refuses it first on every parsed path.

Neither admits the card's defect shape through a stated-judged target; both are candidates for a card.
